Inphinit Proxy

Validation

The Validator is a data validation class that helps minimize the amount of code you will need to write.

Experimental: This is an experimental feature being considered for inclusion and may be subject to change or refactoring

Validating

Validating POST:

use Inphinit\Experimental\Validation\Validator; $validator = Validator::post(); $validator->field('name', $name, 'required|min:5|max:15|regex:/^\S+$/'); $validator->field('surname', $surname, 'min:5|max:50'); // strings with yes, true e 1 returns bool(true) // strings with no, false e 0 returns bool(false) // Outros valores retornam null $validator->field('active', $active, 'required|bool'); if ($validator->valid()) { echo 'Nome: ', htmlentities($name); if ($surname !== null) { echo ' ', htmlentities($surname); } echo '<br>'; echo $active ? '✔️' : '❌'; } else { foreach ($validator->failures() as $failure) { echo '<div class="error"><p>', $failure, '</p></div>'; } }

Validating GET:

use Inphinit\Experimental\Validation\Validator; $validator = Validator::get(); $validator->field('query', $query, 'min:5'); $validator->field('type', $type, 'in:electronics,motors,fashion,sports'); $validator->field('sold', $sold, 'bool'); if ($validator->valid()) { ... }

Validating Arrays and JSONs

use Inphinit\Experimental\Validation\Validator; $arr = [ 'foo' => [ 'bar' => [ 'baz' => '...', ] ] ]; $validator = new Validator($arr); $validator->field('foo.bar.baz', $phone, 'required|regex:/^(?:55)?([1-9]{2})(9?[2-9]\d{3}\d{4})$/'); if ($validator->valid()) { ... }
use Inphinit\Http\Request; use Inphinit\Experimental\Validation\Validator; $app->action('POST', '/receive', function () { $body = file_get_contents('php://input'); if (strlen($body) < 1) { Request::status(400); return 'Invalid request'; } $decoded = json_decode($body, true); if (json_last_error() !== JSON_ERROR_NONE || is_array($body) === false) { Request::status(400); return 'Invalid body'; } $validator = new Validator($decoded); ... });

Validation rules

Before validation, the values are converted to strings:

Rule Combinations Description
bool It can be combined within String values such as yes, true, 1, no, false, and 0
decimal It can be combined with in, regex, min, max Validates whether the field received a decimal number string. The separator can be adjusted using: decimal:., decimal:, , decimal:'
digit It can be combined with in, regex, min, max Validates whether the field received a string written as an integer.
email It can be combined with in, regex, min, max Validate URL usingFILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL
equal:<field name> Compares the field with another field. This can be useful for comparing a password field with a confirmation field.
in: It can be combined with in, regex, min, maxandrequired Checks if the field value is one of the values in the list, for example:in:foo,bar,baz
max:<n> If used with decimal`e` and `rm` digit, it will directly compare the value of the field campo <= max; for the other rules, it will compare the number of characters. strlen(campo) <= max
min:<n> If used with decimal`e` and `rm` digit, it will directly compare the value of the field campo >= min; for the other rules, it will compare the number of characters. strlen(campo) >= min
regex:<n> Validates the field with a custom regular expression, for example:regex:/^[A-Z]+$/
required It can be combined with all rules. Make the field mandatory.
url It can be combined with in, regex, min, maxandrequired Validates URL using FILTER_VALIDATE_URLand checking if the scheme is httpsorhttp

Customizing messages

By default, error messages are in English, but it is possible to modify and configure them with any language system you use, such as Gettext...

The first %scontains the name or path of the field. As for messages containing more than one %s, the following explanations apply:

Message Standard Notice
bool On, Yes, True, 1, Off, No, False, and 0
decimal decimal format
email a valid email
equals not matches with %s
in unexpected value
integer integer format
max maximum %s of %s
min minimum %s of %s
regex not match with the expected format
required is required
type unexpected type
unicode_error invalid Unicode characters It's not part of the validation, but in cases where a field has problematic characters, this is handled as one of the failures, rather than an exception, to avoid code breakage.
url a valid url

Example of customization with gettext:

$validator = Validator::post(); $validator->setMessage('bool', _('boolId')); $validator->setMessage('decimal', _('decimalId')); $validator->setMessage('int', _('intId')); $validator->setMessage('email', _('emailId')); $validator->setMessage('integer', _('inId')); $validator->setMessage('max', _('maxId')); $validator->setMessage('min', _('minId')); $validator->setMessage('regex', _('regexId')); $validator->setMessage('required', _('requiredId')); $validator->setMessage('type', _('typeId')); $validator->setMessage('unicode_error', _('unicode_errorId')); $validator->setMessage('url', _('urlId'));

The file .poshould contain something like:

msgid "boolId" msgstr "O valor deve ser yes ou no." msgid "decimalId" msgstr "O valor deve ser um número decimal."

Extended rules

In addition to the standard rules, Inphinit provides a number of additional rules, extending support:

Rule Combinations Description
cnpj Validates CNPJ (Brazil) in numeric dd.ddd.ddd/dddd-ddand alpha-numeric format AA.ADD.DAD/DDDD-DD(IN RFB 2.229/2024).
cpf Validates CPF (Brazil).
cpfcnpj It verifies whether it's a CPF (Brazilian individual taxpayer registration number) or CNPJ (Brazilian company taxpayer registration number), allowing both.
ip Validate IP
password in, regex, min, max Validate passwords

Para customizar as mensagens de uma regra extendida use o método Validator::getRuleInstange():

$validator->getRuleInstance('ip')->setMessage('default', 'Enter a valid IP'); $validator->getRuleInstance('password') ->setMessage('lower', 'Enter at least one lowercase character.') ->setMessage('special', 'Enter at least one special character.') ->setMessage('upper', 'Enter at least one uppercase character.');

Creating your own rules

It is possible to create your own rules by defining classes that extend Inphinit\Experimental\Validation\Rule:

<?php namespace Foo; use Inphinit\Experimental\Validation\Rule; class BarRule extends Rule { private $messages = array( 'default' => 'Invalid', ); public function exec($path, &$value, array $params, array $rules) { parent::exec($path, $value, $params, $rules); if ($value === 'AAA') { return true; } $this->failure = $this->messages['default']; return false; } }

Uso:

use Inphinit\Http\Response; use Inphinit\Http\Status; $validator->setRule('sample1', Foo\BarRule::class); $validator->setRule('sample2', Foo\BazRule::class); $validator->field('fieldA', $var1, 'sample1'); $validator->field('fieldB', $var2, 'sample1'); if ($validador->valid()) { echo json_encode(['response' => true]); } else { Response::status(Status::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST); echo json_encode($validators->failures()); }
